package main

// CHAOS-5156: lizard's condition_counter is purely token-based, not
// syntax-aware -- a bare "?" token counts as a condition even though Go
// has no ternary operator and "?" is not valid Go syntax anywhere
// outside a string/comment. This fixture exists so goConditions["?"]
// has a GENUINE (non-string, non-comment) token exercising it -- codex
// round r3 on #2266 found that basic.go.txt's own backtick-string
// negative-test fixture (containing "if"/"&&"/"||"/"?" specifically so
// a real miscount would be caught) was ITSELF the only thing satisfying
// "?" coverage, via the coverage scan's own tokenizer not knowing Go's
// backtick-string syntax -- fixed in clike_parity_test.go
// (filteredCorpusTokenPattern); this fixture closes the resulting real
// gap the fix exposed. Since neither lizard nor this port parses real Go
// grammar (both are regex-tokenizer + state-machine only), a
// deliberately non-compiling expression containing a bare "?" is the
// only way to produce a genuine "?" token in valid... well, in
// TOKENIZABLE Go source. Measured directly against real lizard 1.23.0:
// complexity 3 (base 1 + if + ?-as-token).
func questionToken() int {
	if true {
		return 1
	}
	x := 0 ? 1
	return x
}
